newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish villagers to step up gold mine protest.
newsitem.headline: Turkish villagers to step up gold mine protest.

text.p: Villagers in western Turkey are planning to step up protests next week against the opening of a gold mine near the coastal town of Bergama, state-run Anatolian news agency said on Wednesday.

The protesters plan a demonstration in Bergama to follow up a protest last week by a crowd of 3,000-5,000, which blocked a road between Izmir and Canakkale provinces in opposition to the mine opening.

The Turkish Environment Ministry in March approved plans for the mine, owned by Eurogold Madencilik A.S., a subsidiary of the Australian-French venture Mine Or SA and Inmet Mining Corporation of Canada.

"Life in Bergama will come to a halt on Monday. All Turkey will hear our voice, including the officials in Ankara and the officials in our region who cooperated with Eurogold," village chief Hayrettin Cimen said in a statement quoted by Anatolian.
Sixteen village chiefs from the area have visited Bergama council leader Sefa Taskin to seek his support for the November 25 protest against the government's decision to grant a licence.
The gold mine in Ovacik village, 12 km (seven miles) from Bergama, is expected to produce 110,000 ounces of gold annually.
The mine has been opposed because of concerns about the environmental impact of cyanide used in the extraction of gold and because of the felling of olive trees.
Protesters say the possible leakage of cyanide into drinking water and soil could destroy the terrain or have carcinogenic effects.
